Hi Tom / Nimbus security team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear requirements on network isolation and auditability. Below is a short recap of what we covered and concrete next steps so your procurement and infra teams can evaluate options side-by-side.

Recap (high level)
- Primary ask: private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with strong network isolation, optional air-gapped mode for high-risk workloads.
- Compliance constraints: SOC 2 Type II in progress (expected Q3 report), HIPAA controls required for PHI flows, GDPR data residency for some EU tenants (not in scope for US-only deployment).
- Evidence & controls needed: encryption at rest & in transit, KMS integration or HSM, audit logs (immutable), documented retention policy, penetration test reports.

What Redwood can provide (summary)
- SOC2: we have a scoped SOC 2 assessment underway; will share the summary and bridge letter (see attachment).
- Network: for VPC deployments we support tenant-dedicated subnets, strict SGs, and NAT-less egress. For on-prem/air-gapped we provide an installer bundle + guidance for isolated compute and controlled data import/export paths.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS support (AWS KMS/Google KMS) or HSM integration for Private deployments.
- Auditability: per-request tracing, tokenized request IDs, and configurable retention for logs (30/90/365 days).

Immediate next steps (requested items from Nimbus)
1) Nimbus to complete the vendor security questionnaire (I attached a baseline we can pre-fill).
2) Nimbus infra to share an internal network diagram and preferred connectivity pattern (VPC peering, PrivateLink, or on-prem airgap ingestion flow) — Jordan can draft recommended diagrams once we see yours.
3) Confirm whether PHI will be processed in the initial scope (impacts encryption-at-rest and BAA conversation).

Attachments in this email: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary, not full report), vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx (baseline), deployment-diagram-v2.png (sample architecture).

Jordan/Monica — flagging you for architecture and evidence handoff: Jordan, can you prepare a short two-slide decision matrix (VPC vs on-prem vs air-gap) and a checklist of the evidence Nimbus will need to accept us for their environment?

Tom / Nimbus — can you confirm timelines for completing the questionnaire and sharing your internal diagram? We propose a follow-up on Thursday to go over the questionnaire answers.

Best,

Tom / Rafael — quick follow-up with concrete patterns for air-gap updates.

On the air-gapped deployments we typically recommend a pull-based update mechanism initiated from an approved bastion in the isolated network. Pattern options:
1) Signed artifact bundles (recommended): Redwood publishes signed model/artifact bundles to a secure artifact repo. Nimbus downloads the bundle via an operator-initiated pull from the isolated environment using a jump-host (no inbound internet allowed). Bundle contains signed checksum and version metadata.
2) Controlled egress window: scheduled, firewall-limited egress windows to a pre-approved endpoint with strict mutual TLS and IP allowlist. Used for telemetry-only exports, with additional tokenization and rate limits.
3) Manual import: air-gap operator transfers artifacts via removable media (SCP over controlled host) — heavy control but highest isolation.

For telemetry, we recommend local buffering and encrypted batched exports during controlled egress windows; all telemetry is redacted of raw PHI by default (we ship a redaction preprocessor).

Attached is a quick one-page decision matrix and a slightly updated deployment diagram that reflects the pull-based pattern. Also included: a checklist of the SOC2 evidence items Nimbus asked about.
